blocks.text: Re: Kickoff, Roadway Widening Study for Evans-Lee

We are starting the roadway widening study for {{fact:f:E-2005-001.client}}. The aim is a clear report that says what the widening of the corridor requires and what it will cost, backed by work the client can rely on. This memo sets out who carries what and where we begin.

The deliverable is a written report with a recommendation and a concept-level opinion of cost. It is a study, not a construction set. Nothing we draw here goes out under seal until the study is finished and the report is reviewed.

We begin the study on {{fact:f:E-2005-001.start}}. James Skinner, the General Manager at Evans-Lee, is the client's contact. Route anything we need from the owner through Linda George, so the firm speaks to the client with one voice.

The study runs about four months. That is workable for a corridor of this size if we keep the base clean and settle it before we test options on it. We lose the time by drawing options on a base that later has to move.

The work divides the way we usually split a study of this size. Linda George leads it and owns the roadway geometry, the grading, and the coordination with the client. I build the base sheets and the exhibits and keep the utility and drainage information current on them.

items: Existing conditions and base sheets: Jeffrey Perez. I compile the survey, the right-of-way records, and the utility records, and set the base sheet the study is drawn on.
Roadway geometry and grading: Linda George. Linda sets the design controls and the widening options and carries the client coordination.
Drainage and utility checks: shared. Linda sets the approach; I test each option against the drainage and the utilities in the corridor and flag the conflicts.
Cost opinion and report: Linda George, with my exhibits. Linda writes the recommendation; I prepare the figures and the report exhibits.

blocks.text: A widening study is only as good as the record it rests on. So the first effort goes to the survey, the right-of-way, and the utility records, and we will not test an option until that base is confirmed. Check every callout against the design memoranda, not against memory.

Everything gets logged to the project folder as it comes in. The survey, the record prints, and the utility information go to the lettered folder, and each base sheet references the memorandum that governs it. Keep the folder current, so the exhibits at the end are built on filed information and not on loose prints.

Linda George will confirm the design controls and the corridor limits with the client. I will pull the survey and the records and stand up the base sheet. Once the base is confirmed, we lay out the widening options and begin the drainage and utility checks.
The first step is mine. I will have the base sheet and the record set assembled for Linda George to review by the end of the week.
